title: Easement Right in Bangladesh Under Easements Act
metaTitle: Easement Right in Bangladesh Under Easements Act
metaDescription: Learn how easement rights protect passage, drainage, and sunlight under Bangladesh's Easements Act 1882, including 20-year proof, lawsuits, and injunctions.
heroIntro: Under Section 4 of the Easements Act 1882, an easement right entitles a landowner to use an adjacent property for passage, water drainage, or natural light and air. Section 15 grants prescriptive easements after twenty years of uninterrupted enjoyment, while courts enforce blocked access through mandatory injunctions.

quickAnswer.text: Protected civil property rights enforceable in Civil Judge Courts.

sections.title: What Easement Right Means Under the Easements Act 1882
sections.content:
An easement is a non-possessory property right attached to dominant land that restricts how an adjoining servient owner uses their plot. Under Section 4 of the Easements Act 1882, the property benefiting from passage, drainage, or sunlight is called the dominant heritage, while the neighboring parcel bearing that burden is the servient heritage.

Unlike full ownership or co-sharer possession tested in partition suits and boundary demarcation, an easement does not transfer title to the soil. Instead, Section 12 ensures the dominant owner enjoys beneficial occupation—such as crossing a pathway to reach a main road or discharging rainwater through an established drain.

Where neighbors erect sudden brick walls across shared lanes, owners often confuse private civil easements with public nuisance actions under Section 133 CrPC public path clearance. Knowing whether your lane appears on a public mouza map or serves solely private plots determines whether you petition an Executive Magistrate or file a civil title and injunction suit before an Assistant Judge. Reviewing your land mutation and khatian records alongside adjacent boundaries early clarifies this critical distinction before formal civil litigation begins.

sections.title: Key Types of Easements and Statutory Requirements
sections.content:
Bangladesh law recognizes easements by prescription, easements of necessity upon partition, and quasi-easements created when single estates are divided. Section 15 requires open, peaceable, uninterrupted enjoyment as of right for twenty years ending within two years prior to filing suit, whereas Section 13 creates an immediate easement of necessity whenever a sale, gift, or inheritance partition leaves an interior plot completely landlocked.

Easement CategoryStatutory BasisCore Legal ThresholdPrimary Remedy
Prescriptive Right of Way / LightEasements Act 1882, Sec. 1520 years peaceable, open user (60 yrs vs. Govt.)Declaration and injunction under Sec. 35
Easement of NecessityEasements Act 1882, Sec. 13Plot severed with zero alternative accessMandatory declaration against co-sharers/buyers
Substantial Light & Air ObstructionEasements Act 1882, Sec. 28 & 33Physical nuisance materially diminishing habitabilityMandatory demolition injunction (Sec. 55 SRA)
Customary Rural Path / GraveyardEasements Act 1882, Sec. 18Ancient, certain local village customRepresentative civil suit

Note that Section 47 extinguishes an easement after twenty consecutive years of non-enjoyment or permanent release by deed, making prompt legal action essential once obstruction starts.

sections.title: How to Prove a Blocked Path or Light Dispute in Court
sections.content:
Proving an easement claim requires objective survey evidence showing continuous historical access or strict necessity, rather than mere permissive neighborly courtesy. Under the Specific Relief Act 1877 Sections 54 and 55 alongside Order 39 CPC, courts inspect physical site conditions before ordering demolition of an illegal wall.

  1. Serve a Formal Legal Notice: Dispatch a lawyer's legal notice demanding removal of the obstruction within seven to fifteen days and preserving proof of delivery.
  2. File for Declaration and Mandatory Injunction: Submit a plaint before the competent Assistant Judge Court claiming easement rights under Section 15 or Section 13 of the Easements Act 1882.
  3. Seek Local Inspection (Order 26 Rule 9 CPC): Apply immediately for an Advocate Commissioner local investigation to document wall placement, drain alignment, and lack of alternative access.
  4. Establish Twenty-Year Enjoyment or Severance: Present mouza maps, municipal building plans, registered deeds or power of attorney chains, and elderly neighbor testimony proving non-permissive user.

Where urgent construction threatens total blockade, pursuing interim relief similar to stopping unlawful land encroachment prevents irreversible brickwork during trial.

sections.title: Documents Checklist for Filing an Easement Suit
sections.content:
Accurate cadastral maps and unbroken title deeds allow the Civil Court to grant urgent interim protection before a neighbor completes permanent construction. Gather the following verifiable records prior to drafting your civil plaint:

  • Certified CS, SA, RS, and BS Khatian copies alongside the relevant Mauza map showing existing pathways or water channels.
  • Registered Sale Deeds, Heba deeds, or Partition Deeds proving dominant estate ownership and historical severance of adjoining plots.
  • Approved RAJUK, City Corporation, or Pourashava building sanction plans demonstrating setbacks, windows, and drainage outlets.
  • Date-stamped photographs, video footage, and any previous municipal complaint or local arbitration records documenting the obstruction.
  • Affidavits or contact particulars of two to three senior neighboring landowners familiar with the past twenty years of access.
  • For expatriate owners managing property remotely, a properly embassy-attested authorization and verified court affidavit supporting non-resident representation.

Because stamp and court fees depend on suit valuation under the Court Fees Act, confirm the exact assessment beforehand; official figures are indicative only, and the court's official fee schedule governs.

sections.title: Legal Strategy and Chamber Consultation
sections.content:
Delaying civil action after a pathway is walled off risks losing interim status-quo relief and strengthens a neighbor's plea of abandonment under Section 47 of the Easements Act 1882. Because defendants routinely argue that passage was only temporary permissive license rather than an adverse prescriptive right, drafting precise pleadings grounded in Sections 13, 15, and 35 alongside a timely Order 39 injunction petition is decisive for preserving access pending full trial.

faqs.question: How many years are required to prove a prescriptive easement right in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Under Section 15 of the Easements Act 1882, you must prove open, peaceable, uninterrupted enjoyment of the pathway, drain, or light as of right for at least twenty consecutive years over private property, or sixty years against government land, ending within two years prior to filing suit.

faqs.question: Can I claim a right of way if my neighbor only gave verbal permission?
faqs.answer: No. Permission or neighborly license defeats a prescriptive easement claim under Section 15 because the enjoyment must be exercised openly as an independent right, not by temporary permission. However, if your plot became completely landlocked upon division from a common estate, you may claim an easement of necessity under Section 13.

faqs.question: What happens if a neighbor builds a wall blocking sunlight to my home?
faqs.answer: Under Sections 28, 33, and 35 of the Easements Act 1882, if your windows have enjoyed natural light and air for twenty years and a neighbor's illegal construction causes substantial physical nuisance making rooms uninhabitable, the Civil Court can grant a mandatory injunction ordering modification or demolition.

faqs.question: Should I file a Section 133 CrPC case or a civil suit for a blocked road?
faqs.answer: Section 133 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898 applies strictly to public pathways, municipal lanes, or community drains blocked by unlawful obstruction. If the disputed passage lies entirely inside private land without public dedication, you must file a civil declaration and injunction suit under the Easements Act 1882.

faqs.question: How can an easement right be lost or extinguished under Bangladesh law?
faqs.answer: Under Sections 38 to 47 of the Easements Act 1882, an easement is extinguished if the dominant owner executes a formal release deed, if both dominant and servient lands merge into single ownership, or if the easement remains continuously unused and unenjoyed for twenty consecutive years.
